newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia minister resigns amid probes.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia minister resigns amid probes.

text.p: Embattled British Columbia Education Minister Moe Sihota said Thursday he was resigning pending the outcome of investigations into allegations of conflict of interest.

"I advised the Premier this morning that I would like to be relieved of my duties for the duration of these reviews, so that I can deal with these frustrating accusations once and for all," Sihota told reporters.
Sihota said he was confident he would be cleared. He has been under attack in recent weeks over several allegations of wrongdoing.
The government said Sihota was merely stepping down while the investigations were conducted. The opposition Liberals demanded that Sihota's resignation be permanent.
Sihota has been under fire for weeks. The most serious allegations against him concerned his friendship with Herb Dhaliwal, now a Liberal member of Parliament.

Sihota has been accused of conflict of interest in appointing Dhaliwal to the board of the provincial utility in 1991 after Dhaliwal guaranteed a mortgage for Sihota. Sihota has also been accused of improperly lobbying the Motor Carrier Commission of behalf of a limousine company owned by Dhaliwal.
The charges are being reviewed by the Premier and the conflict of interest commissioner.
Sihota resigned from the cabinet last year after he was found guilty of professional misconduct as a lawyer, but was reinstated three months later.

The move was the latest blow to the administration of British Columbia Premier Glen Clark who has faced heavy criticism over handling of the government's finances and allegations that his party misled voters in the May election.
